title: Requirement assessment standard
boundary: Human recorded judgments for a named use. Contract checks do not establish semantic sufficiency, ratification, execution permission or fulfillment.

investigation.label: Investigation
investigation.description: A bounded permitted inquiry can proceed while the proposition remains unproven.

checks.label: Clear question and learning
checks.description: The question and intended learning are explicit.

checks.label: Affected context
checks.description: The relevant people, work and conditions are identified.

checks.label: Bounded method
checks.description: The proposed method, limits and responsible next step are stated.

checks.label: Applicable constraints
checks.description: Applicable policy, safety, access and authority constraints are identified without inventing permission.

prototype.label: Bounded prototype/test
prototype.description: A scoped test can examine an unproven proposition without treating it as supported.

checks.label: Hypothesis or question
checks.description: The hypothesis or question being tested is explicit.

checks.label: Target users and context
checks.description: The intended users and test conditions are stated.

checks.label: Test boundaries and constraints
checks.description: The bounded test respects applicable constraints; it does not imply production permission.

checks.label: Observable learning criteria
checks.description: The observations that would support or challenge the hypothesis are defined.

checks.label: Responsible next step
checks.description: A responsible next step is stated without inventing an accepted assignment.

implementation.label: Implementation of the named scope
implementation.description: The named scope has actionable definition, applicable support and resolved material dependencies. This recommendation grants no execution authority.

checks.label: Unambiguous behavior or constraint
checks.description: Behavior or constraint and scope are actionable and consistently interpreted.

checks.label: User and system context
checks.description: Relevant users, systems, conditions and applicability are stated.

checks.label: Material acceptance conditions
checks.description: Observable acceptance conditions include applicable failure and boundary cases.

checks.label: Current applicable basis
checks.description: The material claims have current evidence of the required level and explicit limits.

checks.label: Design, interfaces and dependencies
checks.description: Material design, interface and dependency questions are resolved for this scope; a claim of none needs a grounded explanation.

checks.label: Policy and authority constraints
checks.description: No unresolved non-negotiable constraint violation remains. Risk acceptance or a waiver cannot be invented.

research.implication: Investigate the claim in its actual user and work context; preserve counterevidence and limits.
research.question: What observation would support or challenge this condition, and what does the current evidence leave uncertain?

design.implication: Develop and test the interaction, including failure and boundary conditions relevant to this scope.
design.question: What behavior must the design make observable, and which assumptions or unresolved dependencies should the test examine?

operations.implication: Check how the condition fits operational roles, exceptions, handoffs and existing controls.
operations.question: Who needs to act under which conditions, and what evidence would show that exceptions and handoffs work?

sponsor.implication: Connect the proposed condition to the intended value, scope and applicable business constraints.
sponsor.question: What value or obligation makes this condition material, and what uncertainty would change the direction?

requirement-owner.implication: Keep the definition, acceptance conditions and material dependencies actionable while preserving open questions.
requirement-owner.question: What must be clarified or evidenced for the next intended use, and which decision remains with its accountable owner?

default.implication: Apply the shared standard to your contribution without treating the domain explanation as a new judgment or permission.
default.question: What can your role establish for this condition, and which evidence, limits or questions must travel with the contribution?
